outcome: Give hospital coo / chief medical information officer a governed method to improve avoidable non-attendance rate using booking history, clinic type and consented reminders, with final decisions…
overview: Outpatient No-Show Intervention addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in healthcare providers operations. The first proof of value uses booking history, clinic type and consented reminders. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is avoidable non-attendance rate, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: booking history, clinic type and consented reminders; define avoidable non-attendance rate and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Hospital COO / Chief Medical Information Officer.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
